Issued at 134 AM CDT Thu Oct 22 2026

As high surface pressure is moving to the east over the Great Lakes, 
a low surface pressure will be developing over NV and moving to the 
northeast to be over MT today. This will be causing the pressure 
gradient over SD to tighten, which helps to strengthen the winds 
aloft. These stronger southeasterly winds will start to mix down 
over central SD this afternoon, with gusts up to 30 mph. Overnight 
the stronger winds will spread to the east over northeastern SD and 
west central MN as a low level jet develops over the area. Friday 
morning into the afternoon, the HREF has a 30-50% chance for the 
winds to be gusting up to 45 mph or more along the edges of the 
Prairie Coteau. The ensembles on the other hand keep the chance for 
this below 30%. These winds are right on the edge of wind advisory 
criteria, and the upcoming model runs will need to be watched to see 
if an advisory is needed. These stronger winds and the dry 
vegetation over the area are leading to high grassland fire danger 
over central SD on Thursday and high to very high over central and 
northeastern SD and west central MN. The one thing keeping the fire 
danger from increasing, and a red flag warning being needed, is the 
higher humidity values. Thursday the minimum relative humidity is 
above 35% and Friday the values east of the Missouri River will be 
above 35% and to the west will be between 30-45%: lowest over Jones, 
Stanley, and Lyman counties. 

While the low surface pressure will not be moving over SD as it 
heads into Canada, its frontal boundaries will. A warm front has 
moved in today and will stick around for a bit Friday. The 
southeasterly winds behind this warm front will move more warmth 
into SD, causing temperatures today and Friday to be 20-25 degrees 
warmer than normal, with highs in the upper 70s to low 80s. Some 
moisture will be moving in Thursday evening and overnight along the 
southeasterly flow. This moisture will interact with the low level 
jet and the warm front moving out on Friday to cause some isolated 
showers Thursday night to scattered rain showers early Friday 
morning into the afternoon over central and northeastern SD. There 
will be another round of rain showers late Friday night into 
Saturday morning as the cold front moves through. The models vary 
how long the front and its rain sits over portions of eastern SD 
Saturday, which then impacts how much rainfall is expected. The HREF 
has a 20-40% chance for 0.1 inch of rain to occur over northeastern 
SD by Friday night while the ensembles have 10-20%. The ensembles 
then have a 20-50% chance for 0.1 inch to occur from both rounds of 
rain from Friday and Saturday combined. So, not much rainfall is 
expected.

The cold front moving through will cause some strong post frontal 
winds to develop over central SD late Friday night into Saturday 
morning. There is a 30-60% chance for winds to be sustained at or 
greater than 30 mph, and 30-60% chance for gusts to be 45 mph or 
more west of the James River Valley. This cold front will also bring 
a substantial change to temperatures by cooling things off again. 
Sunday's temperatures will be around normal to 10 degrees below 
normal for this time of the year, with highs in the mid 40s to low 
50s. 

The next chance for precipitation will then come in Sunday 
afternoon/evening into Monday. This precipitation will be developing 
from a low pressure over CO that had a frontal boundary stretching 
over the central plains. The models show rain developing along this 
frontal boundary and overrunning it to the north into SD. This is 
supported by the upper-level trough moving through the area aloft as 
well as the precipitation being in an entrance region of a jet. 
There is variability in the models as to how far north the rain 
gets, as it will be interacting with the high pressure at the 
surface over ND and SD. Additionally, the models vary the timing, 
track, and rainfall amounts. This will need to be something to keep 
an eye on in upcoming model runs, especially since there will be 
temperatures near freezing Sunday night into Monday morning when 
some of the precipitation could be occurring.
